title: DigCompEdu Check-In | Offer a way in before the task begins

qcReview.basis: Publisher’s English supplement dated 2 June 2023, © Ersoy et al., CC BY 4.0, was verified against the preserved SHA-256. The 3 prompts, 15 ordered options and item weights match the registered area; scoring follows the publication’s 0–4 option order. This independent report uses the project’s complete-response area sum (0–12); the original study reports 22-item total levels and did not validate independent area use. No source grading bands are imported.

interpretations.headline: Offer a way in before the task begins
interpretations.summary:
Before a case discussion, students are asked to annotate a complex digital diagram. Some only have phones, and several are new to the platform. The educator offers an accessible diagram and a simple choice of how to record their reasoning. Everyone answers the same case question and has something to bring to the discussion.

This total describes how you reported anticipating digital barriers, adapting activities for different learners and inviting active participation. Those practices depend partly on device access, formats, and placement or timetable constraints. Consider where students currently spend effort getting into a task before it asks them to think.

guidance.text: Open one required assignment on an ordinary phone or low-bandwidth connection. Ask learners how it works for them. Provide an alternative format or route that still demonstrates the same goal.
Keep the same case question and success criteria. Offer an optional prompt or practice example, then let students choose how to show their reasoning in a way you can review.

This area-only presentation and feedback are project adaptations and imply no author or Commission endorsement.

This English reflection applies to adult higher-education faculty in health sciences. The original study used a convenience sample of 306 faculty members from six partner universities. The standalone area has no separate validation or local norms.

The area sum adds 3 equally weighted 0–4 items. Zero is a valid response; an omitted answer leaves the area result unavailable. No scale-wide total, A1–C2 level, percentile or individual certification is reported.
report.disclaimer: For your own professional learning in health-sciences higher education. This report describes self-reported digital teaching practice and supplies no basis for evaluating teaching performance, ranking faculty, or certifying competence.
